en: The *Sūtra on the Son of Shenri*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra of India during the Song Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the kingdom of Rājagṛha. At that time,
The king, the high ministers, the officials, and the people—none failed to revere those who received the teachings and precepts.

The Buddha instructed the king, the elders, the officials, and the commoners that they must not kill living beings, steal, or violate the wives of others; they must not engage in double-tongued speech, harsh words, lying, or frivolous talk; nor must they harbor jealousy, stinginess, greed, or doubt. They should believe that performing good deeds brings good results and performing evil deeds brings evil results, and that what one does not desire for oneself should not be inflicted upon others.
Those who study other heterodox paths and do not receive the precepts of the Buddha's teaching are no longer respected by kings, elders, officials, or commoners.
The reason they are not respected is that their path is not the True Way; they do not teach others through morality and virtue, but instead kill living beings themselves and incite others to kill;
they steal people’s property themselves and incite others to seize people’s property.
One personally commits adultery with the wives of others and incites others to commit adultery with the wives of others;

one personally engages in double-tongued speech, harsh speech, false speech, and frivolous speech, and incites others to engage in double-tongued speech, harsh speech, false speech, and frivolous speech;
one personally harbors jealousy, stinginess, greed, and doubt, and incites others to harbor jealousy, stinginess, greed, and doubt.
In that country there was an elder of the four castes named Shenri (Śunyata). His wealth was immense, possessing countless amounts of gold, silver, and precious jewels.
Shenri served other paths; he did not serve the Buddha-way and did not believe in the Buddhist scriptures.
The followers of other paths were all envious of the Buddha; they gathered together with Shenri and deliberated, saying:
"The Buddha is now revered by the king, his ministers, the high officials, and the people, whereas we alone are not revered by the king, the border officials, the high officials, or the people."
The Buddha has often said of himself:
"I know the affairs of the past, future, and present; I foresee what others will say and what they think in their hearts.
Now, it would be well to test whether this is truly as the Buddha has said.
Śunika asked, "How should one test this?
Other heterodox practitioners instructed Śunika:
"He prepared a meal to invite the Buddha, placing poison within it;
he dug a pit inside the gate five *zhang* deep, placed fire within it, and covered the top with a thin layer of earth, intending for the Buddha to enter by descending from above."
"If the Buddha truly knew the matters of the past, future, and present, he would not accept an invitation;
that he accepts an invitation is because he does not know the matters of the past, future, and present.
Thereupon, they dug a pit in the ground, prepared a meal, and placed poison within it.
Shenri said, "Yes! Great Joy!"
He immediately went to invite the Buddha.
The Buddha said, "Excellent!"
Śunyata then spoke to the heretics, and the heretics said, "Since this man knows nothing at all, we need only dig a pit in the ground.
Śunyata had a son named Cāṇakya, sixteen years of age, who had studied the Buddha-way in a previous life and was able to know the affairs of the past, future, and present. He said to his father:
"The Buddha already knows the deliberations of other paths; there is no need for testing. Do not follow the words of wicked men and cast yourself into boiling water or fire.
Although Shenri did not believe his son's words, he nevertheless ordered a pit to be dug and placed fire within it, and prepared a meal with which he set poison.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Command all the bhikṣus that tomorrow none shall go before the Buddha; when it is time for the meal, they must all follow behind the Buddha.
As the Buddha sat contemplating the Right Path, all the heavenly kings were stirred with agitation.
Śunika sent a messenger to inform the Buddha:
"The time has arrived; we pray that you will come for the meal.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
“Command the bhikṣus to put on their robes, take up their alms bowls, and follow behind the Buddha.

The bhikṣus received the instruction; they donned their robes, took up their alms bowls, and all followed the Buddha. Countless celestial kings and spirits likewise accompanied the Buddha on his journey.

The Buddha then transformed the ground into gold as far as the gate of Shenri; as he proceeded along the path, he immediately emitted radiance, causing the entire interior of Shenri’s house to turn golden.
Cāṇūra then said to his father:

"Now the Buddha has arisen and set out upon the Path; the ten directions are as bright as the sun. The Buddha, together with the bhikṣus and countless devas, has come forth; the Buddha, together with the bhikṣus and countless devas, moves along like the moon among the stars.
Now, the brightness within your house, father, is just like this!"
"There is no need to test the Buddha.
Shenri did not follow his son's words.

When the Buddha arrived at the city gate and stepped upon the threshold, the entire city shook violently; those who were ill were immediately healed, the blind regained their sight, the deaf regained their hearing, the mute were able to speak, the poisoned were freed from the effects of the venom, the insane regained their composure, the hunchbacked were straightened, and those filled with anger became joyful.

The *konghou* lute played music of its own accord without being struck; the pearl bracelets of the women all produced sounds by themselves; and hundreds of birds, beasts, and animals cried out in harmony with one another in lamentation.

When the Buddha arrived at the gate of Śreṇika, a fire pit five *zhang* deep became a bathing pool, in which lotuses grew—one flower producing a thousand petals, while the flowers trodden upon by the disciples each produced a hundred petals—and they all walked across the tops of these flowers.
When Shenri saw the fire pit transformed into a pond filled with blooming lotuses, he was struck with great terror. Prostrating himself with his head to the ground, he spoke with sincerity:
"I have prepared this meal for the Buddha, yet I have placed poison within it. I pray that you will accept my confession and allow me to prepare a proper meal instead."
The Buddha said, "There is no need to cook again; bring the poisoned rice and eat it.
The Buddha took his seat, and all the bhikṣus sat down as well.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Command the bhikṣus not to eat for now; they shall eat only when the Buddha instructs them.
The Buddha then recited a mantra, saying:
“In the world there are generally three poisons:
first, lustful greed;
second, anger and hatred;”

Third is ignorance. Since the Buddha is free from these three poisons, the poisons do not manifest; likewise, for those who possess the sutras and the Dharma with utmost sincerity, the poisons do not manifest; and for those such as the bhikṣus whose path is correct, the poisons also do not manifest.
As soon as the Buddha had finished speaking, the poison in the food was entirely eliminated.
The Buddha said to Ānanda, “Have all the bhikṣus eat; the poison has already been removed.”

When the Buddha and all the bhikṣus had finished their meal, Shenri (Śinir) immediately stepped forward and knelt with his right knee on the ground. Placing his head at the Buddha’s feet, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“I have acted without propriety; following the words of an evil person, I committed evil deeds. I pray that you, O Buddha, will take pity on me and accept my repentance for these transgressions.”
The Buddha then preached the sutra for Shenri, who immediately attained the first stage of the *srotāpanna* path.
Shenri then received the five precepts and became an *upāsaka*:
first, not to kill;...
Second, not stealing;
third, not violating the wives of others;
fourth, not engaging in double-tongued speech.
Fifth, one shall not drink alcohol.
Having received the five precepts, Shenri placed his head at the Buddha’s feet and paid homage to the Buddha.
[From] *The Original Scripture of Shenri’s Son*.
